indian.headline: Sensex and Nifty fell nearly 1.8% on profit-taking after a four-week rally ended.
indian.lead: Sensex and Nifty fell nearly 1.8% on profit-taking after a four-week rally ended.
indian.brief: Sensex dropped 1.77% and Nifty 50 fell 1.75%, with Bank Nifty down 3.17%, as investors locked in gains following four consecutive weeks of gains.
why: Four-week winning streak prompted profit-booking: investors sold after the Nifty's longest rally in five months, triggering index declines across the board.
Banking stocks led losses with a 3.2% decline, dragging down Bank Nifty by 3.17% despite pharma support, as the sector that drove recent gains reversed.
Metal stocks fell 3.7%, adding to selling pressure alongside energy's 1.8% drop, offsetting mild gains in IT and realty.
indian.narrative:
Indian benchmarks reversed course on 23 November after four straight weeks of gains. The Sensex fell 1.77% while the Nifty 50 dropped 1.75%, signalling a classic profit-booking pullback. The Nifty had closed Friday at 25,800.60, capping its longest winning streak in five months. Banking stocks—which had led the rally—became the biggest casualties, tumbling 3.2% as investors trimmed positions. Bank Nifty fell 3.17%, reflecting the sector's sharp reversal. Metal stocks declined 3.7% and energy fell 1.8%, adding to the downward momentum.

Underneath the near-term selling lay a bullish longer-term backdrop. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have turned aggressive buyers, purchasing ₹1.18 lakh crore worth of Indian equities in November alone and ₹1.22 lakh crore cumulatively, pushing the Sensex up 20% in dollar terms. This strong FPI inflow reflects confidence despite today's pullback. Meanwhile, structural market developments—including Shriram Finance's upcoming entry into the Sensex (replacing Trent on 21 December) and multiple IPO launches, including Foodlink's on 26 November—suggest sustained investor interest in Indian equities. The profit-taking is viewed as a natural pause in a longer uptrend supported by foreign money.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: FPI inflows remain strong at ₹1.22 lakh crore YTD; rupee expected to strengthen to 91.50/$ if momentum holds.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: FPIs have turned aggressive buyers; ₹1.18 lakh crore invested in November alone amid strong equity inflows.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Energy sector fell 1.8% today; no fresh price data, but sector weakness suggests downward pressure.

indian.watch: Whether foreign inflows sustain next week or if profit-booking deepens; Foodlink IPO opens 26 November.

us.headline: US stocks sink as tech crashes 7.3%; traders cut Fed rate-hike bets to 95% after 10% correction.
us.lead: US stocks sink as tech crashes 7.3%; traders cut Fed rate-hike bets to 95% after 10% correction.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 3.70%, Nasdaq dropped 5.28%, and Dow slipped 1.93% in a broad market retreat.
why: Tech sector plunged 7.3% — the steepest decline among all sectors — dragging the Nasdaq down 5.28% as growth stocks face pressure.
US stock markets entered 'correction' territory (down over 10% from recent peaks), triggering a flight to safety and reducing bets on aggressive Fed rate hikes from earlier expectations to 95%.
Dollar eased off 19-month highs as investors repriced expectations for less aggressive monetary policy, signaling a shift in sentiment toward lower rates ahead.
China's AI sector collapsed with $1.7 trillion in losses, raising global concerns about tech valuations and competitive pressures in AI chips.
us.narrative:
US markets suffered a sharp selloff on 23 November, with the Nasdaq hit hardest as the Technology sector collapsed 7.3%. The S&P 500 retreated 3.70% and the Dow fell 1.93%, reflecting broad weakness across equities. After last week's slide pushed stocks into 'correction' territory — a standard 10%+ pullback from recent highs — traders recalibrated their Federal Reserve rate-hike bets to 95%, down from earlier hawkish expectations. The dollar weakened off its 19-month peak as the market repriced for a more measured Fed path.

Sector pain was uneven: Financials fell 1.8%, Energy dropped 0.6%, and Healthcare edged down just 0.1%. The selloff reflects growing worries about AI valuations, particularly after China's AI stocks hemorrhaged $1.7 trillion in value this year. Meanwhile, long-term tailwinds remain intact—Goldman Sachs forecasts gold at $4,650 by end-2027, global electrical infrastructure spending is set to hit $32 trillion over the next decade, and India's semiconductor push (Semicon 2.0) is attracting real capital. Amazon's $7.5 billion bid for AI software firm Decart shows the race to compete with Nvidia heating up despite near-term tech pain.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Nasdaq −5.28%; worst-performing sector of the day.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Traders now expect less aggressive policy tightening.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Stocks in correction; dollar weakens; growth under pressure.

us.watch: Watch Fed rate-cut timeline; China AI recovery signals; and earnings for guidance on AI spending sustainability.
